one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 2026 results, expected around 2026-10-20/21 (Q2 was reported 2026-07-21; date not yet confirmed). Q3 revenue is already pre-announced at >30% sequential growth (>~$186M) [9], so the headline is known. What moves the stock is (a) how much of the Q3 royalty jump (I estimate royalties >= ~$60M vs ~$30M in Q2) is a catch-up for past VPD shipments rather than run-rate, (b) Q4 guidance and product (ex-royalty) gross margin, which slipped in Q2 [2], and (c) any update on new licensees or the second fab. Hyperscaler Q3 capex guides (late October) also fall in the window and the capex file expects them to stay supportive [22]. Against that, the stock has risen ~66% from $183.91 on 2026-09-16 [10] in under three weeks on two guidance raises, which raises short-term reversal risk, and in July it fell on a beat because operating income declined y/y [5]. On balance I centre the month slightly below spot (median ~$300) with the stock's usual monthly volatility (95%/3.5 ~ 27%), and do not take a strong directional view.

fair_value.method: Blend of SOTP (product earnings at the peer-median 32x plus recurring royalties at 20x plus net cash) $186, P/E on CY2028E EPS $6.50 x 32x = $209, and a DCF reaching $2.0B revenue by 2031 at 11% WACC = $150; weights 0.45/0.35/0.20 give ~$187 for Oct-2027.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Product: CY2028E product revenue $850M, product GM 55%, ~90% of opex $270M -> product EBIT ~$225M + interest $15M, 20% tax -> $4.00/sh x 32x = $128. Recurring royalties: CY2028E ~$180M less ~$30M IP/legal cost, 20% tax -> $2.50/sh x 20x = $50. Net cash after fab-2 spending ~ $8/sh. Total ~$186. One-off catch-up royalties and settlements excluded.

inputs_detail.value: $30.4M, of which $15M from the new Q2 licence (recognition front-loaded; $5M in Q3, then $10M/qtr for 4 qtrs, $60M total)
2023 $15.9M, 2024 $46.6M, 2025 $57.4M; Q1-26 $15.0M; plus a one-off $45M patent settlement in Q2 2025
~$61M royalties: ~$15M legacy, $5M Q2-licence, ~$41M first VPD licence, of which ~$20M treated as one-off catch-up
inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 revenue $186M less product ~$125M (Q2 $112.9M + double-digit advanced-products growth guided [2]) = ~$61M royalties. VPD licence signed mid-September yet already worth ~$40M in the quarter, which implies some past-use catch-up; I treat half as one-off (judgment, not disclosed).

2026 product ~ $470M (Q1 ~$98M, Q2 $112.9M, Q3 ~$125M, Q4 ~$135M); Fab 1 output target $1B/yr rising to >=$1.5B [11], fab 2 not before late 2027/2028 [7]; ~30% CAGR, below consensus total revenue 2027 $979M [14] because I strip one-off royalties.

Q2 GM $83.1M less ~$30M royalty at ~100% margin leaves ~$52.7M on $112.9M product = ~47% [1]; product margin fell on fab restructuring [2]; I assume scale lifts it to 55%, below the 70% long-term total-company target.
Q2 GM $83.1M less operating income $34.9M = $48.2M/qtr [1]; grown ~18%/yr for fab-2 start-up, R&D and IP enforcement.

VPD licence ~$110M/yr run-rate (volume-based, raised again 2026-09-30 [9]) + legacy/OEM licences ~$50M after Q2-licence fixed payments end mid-2028 + ~$20M. Licences are ~2-year terms with renewal flexibility [2]; LEO-driven settlements were sized at ~$300M through 2026 [12].
Peer median forward P/E 32.1x (11 peers, StockAnalysis forward basis). No premium: see comps_summary.

Below Rambus 32.5x [29] and far below Arm [30]: Vicor's royalties come from short (~2-year) litigation-driven licences backed by an ITC exclusion order, are concentrated in a handful of licensees and the 10-K gives no renewal assurance [3][2].

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: CY2028E EPS $6.50 (product $4.00 + recurring royalty $2.50) x 32.1x peer-median forward P/E = $209 (the forward basis at the Oct-2027 horizon).

inputs_detail.derivation: Sum of SOTP product and royalty EPS. Cross-check: consensus CY2027 EPS $6.12 [14]; my CY2027 is ~$5.37 because I exclude catch-up and assume a 20% normalised tax rate (TTM GAAP net income $145M exceeds TTM EBITDA $115M because of tax credits/benefits, including a $14.3M CHIPS ITC refund [2][15]).
Peer median forward P/E (Vertiv); VICR trades at 56.3x on the same basis [15].

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue 2027-31 $850M/1,050/1,350/1,700/2,000M; EBIT margin 36%->40% (mgmt LT target 40%); tax 20%; capex incl. fab 2 $150/220/180/120/130M; WACC 11%; terminal growth 4%; + $450M cash; 47.8M shares -> $135 today, ~$150 at horizon.

inputs_detail.value: $2.5B revenue, 70% GM, 40% operating margin; needs a second fab

inputs_detail.derivation: Reaches 80% of the $2.5B target by 2031, since fab 2 arrives late 2027/2028 at the earliest [7] and Fab 1 tops out at ~$1-1.5B [11].
High-beta small-mid cap, 95% realised vol, customer concentration [3]; no debt [15].
Two properties bought (334k sq ft building + 54 acres) [17]; phased 2-3x Fab 1 capacity [7]; Q2 capex $11.2M/qtr today [1].

bear.story: Q3/Q4 show the VPD royalty was largely catch-up; legacy 2-year licences renew at lower rates or lapse; MPS/Infineon-Delta/ADI-Empower VPD modules win sockets (the licence lets the OEM buy from unlicensed suppliers [21]), so Vicor taxes the socket but does not win the product; the lead wafer-scale customer's orders slow; multiple compresses to the peer median on ~$4.40 EPS.

base.story: Product grows ~30%/yr within Fab 1 limits, royalties settle at ~$180M/yr recurring, EPS heads to ~$6.50 in 2028; the multiple compresses from 56x towards ~37x as royalty quality is questioned and AI-capex growth slows in 2028 per the capex file's base case [22].

bull.story: The second ITC case and VPD exclusion risk push more hyperscalers to license; royalties pass $300M/yr; 2nd-gen VPD wins at hyperscalers; fab 2 on track; 2028 EPS ~$10 at ~48x.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 21.9x (AEIS) to 127.0x (ARM), interquartile ~26-46x; forward EV/EBITDA 16.8x (IFX) to 244.9x (ARM), median 28.0x. All P/E figures are StockAnalysis forward P/E on 2026-10-05. Forward EV/EBITDA is derived as TTM EV/EBITDA / (1 + consensus next-FY revenue growth), i.e. it assumes a constant EBITDA margin, because no free source publishes forward EBITDA for all peers (ADI growth derived from EPS, Delta assumed 30%).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: VICR trades at 56.3x forward P/E and ~95x derived forward EV/EBITDA (EV $13.64B / TTM EBITDA $114.8M / 1.2), about 1.75x the peer median P/E. We apply the peer median 32x to product earnings and 20x (below the range median) to royalty earnings; the blended multiple on CY2028E EPS is ~28x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. VICR's consensus EPS growth (2027 +49% [14]) beats the peer median (~36%), but the gap mostly reflects royalties, and their durability is the weakest part of the story: ~2-year licence terms, a few licensees, and dependence on ITC exclusion orders. Product-only gross margin (~47% in Q2) is below MPWR/ADI. Vicor has a single fab, is capacity-constrained until late 2027/2028, and has a record of losing a major GPU socket to MPS (H100) after claiming design wins [18]. Majority advanced-products revenue comes from one or a few customers [3]. No evidence supports a premium that would persist to Oct-2027, so we discount the royalty stream and keep the product business at the median.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$150, which is below the Sept-16 pre-licence level of $184 and near my bear case, the market would be saying that the VPD royalty stream is not recurring (mostly catch-up, or the licensee sourcing collapses) and/or that the product ramp has failed (lost the lead accelerator customer or a 2nd-gen VPD hyperscaler socket). That is a fundamental break, not ordinary 95%-vol noise. Conversely, if the stock holds above ~$300 while Q3/Q4 confirm >$40M/qtr recurring VPD royalties, my skeptic fair value is too low.

key_uncertainties: Recurring vs one-off royalty: Q3 2026 VPD royalty (~$40M by my estimate) is not split by Vicor into catch-up and run-rate; this alone swings fair value by ~$50/share.
Licence durability: ~2-year terms, a handful of licensees, dependence on ITC exclusion orders; PTAB has so far upheld Vicor patents against Delta (2024) [13] but new challenges are possible.
Competition in VPD from MPS, Infineon+Delta and ADI (Empower) [19][20]; the VPD licence lets the OEM buy from unlicensed suppliers, so royalties may substitute for product share.
Customer concentration: the lead customer's wafer-scale AI engine ramp (an ~11% customer in 2025) [3][11].

Defense/aerospace share is not disclosed: the FY2025 10-K gives no A&D percentage [3]; management says A&D business with key customers is 'a larger multiple' of past years [2] and that geopolitics is driving growth [11]. A&D sits mainly in Brick Products, which were ~39% of 2025 revenue and $49.2M (34%) in Q2 2026 [1]. My judgment is that A&D is roughly 10-20% of revenue, and this is unverified.
Normalised tax rate: GAAP EPS has been inflated by tax credits (CHIPS ITC refund $14.3M) [2]; TTM net income exceeds TTM EBITDA [15].
AI capex cycle: the capex file's base case still grows 2027 customer capex ~50% but 2028 risk is skewed down for some suppliers [22].
reasoning: VICR is a $14.1B company (46.1M shares, $446M net cash) at $305.61, trading at 56x consensus forward EPS and ~29x EV/TTM sales after a +525% year [15]. Since 2026-09-16 the stock has risen from $184 on a first VPD licence and two Q3 guidance raises (Q3 revenue >$186M, +30% q/q) that management attributes to royalties [9][21]. The skeptic case: (1) A large and growing share of revenue and an even larger share of profit is royalty. Royalties were $30.4M of $143.4M in Q2 (21%) and I estimate ~$61M of ~$186M in Q3, at ~100% margin. These royalties come from litigation-driven, ~2-year licences, with a fixed $60M schedule on the Q2 deal and $45M one-off settlement in 2025, so the market should not capitalise them like product earnings. (2) Product-only gross margin is ~47% and slipped in Q2. Operating income fell y/y in Q2 and the stock dropped on a beat [5]. (3) Capacity: one fab, with a second not before late 2027/2028 and ~$0.5B of capex to come [7]. (4) Competition: MPS, Infineon/Delta and ADI/Empower are all pushing VPD [19][20]. Vicor lost NVIDIA H100 to MPS after promising wins [18]. The new licence explicitly lets the OEM buy VPD modules from unlicensed rivals [21]. (5) Governance and flow: the CEO holds ~44% with insiders and sells under 10b5-1 (0 insider buys vs 192 sales in 6 months) [4][15]; short interest is ~8% of float [15]; Needham cut its target to $320 in July [16]. Weighed honestly, the bull points are real. The PTAB rejected Delta's IPRs [13], hyperscalers are approaching Vicor for licences, the Sep-30 raise reflects higher volume-based royalties (the stream scales with AI deployments), the backlog is $380M (+145% y/y) [1], and the capex file's base case has customer AI capex rising ~50% in 2027 [22]. Separating one-off from recurring royalties and valuing each part, I get a fair value of ~$187 (SOTP $186, P/E $209, DCF $150), about 40% below spot. The peer set (11 AI-power, power-semi and IP-licensing names) has a forward P/E median of 32x, and I find no persistent quality advantage to justify VICR's 75% premium. The ladder is not centred on fair value, because multiples converge slowly and AI-power peers are themselves rich. Scenarios: bear $140 (30%), base $240 (45%), bull $480 (25%), mean ~$270. The ladder uses a lognormal with median ~$242 and sigma ~0.62, below the 95% trailing realised vol because some of that vol came from a re-rating that has now happened. P(>= spot $306) ~35%, P(>= $183) ~67%, P(>= $611) ~6.5%. Limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate and insider endpoints were unavailable (plan/rate limits), so consensus and peer data come from StockAnalysis pages. A search on recent named-insider sales was blocked by my privacy rule and not repeated. Fewer than 60% of sources are in-lane because the brief's required 11-peer comps table needs 11 data sources; 14 of 33 sources are in-lane skeptic material, and the PTAB, SemiAnalysis, goldesel and iTiger items are unlikely to be found by other lanes. No option data was used.
